::: {#rem-bits-nats}
#### Converting between bits and nats

For any probability $p \in (0, 1]$,
the change-of-base rule for logarithms gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
-\log_2 p
&= \frac{-\ln p}{\ln 2}\\
&\approx 1.443 \times (-\ln p).
\end{aligned}
$$

So an outcome with a surprisal of $1$ nat has a surprisal of
$1 / \ln 2 \approx 1.443$ bits.

A bit as a unit of information is not the same thing as
a bit as a binary digit.
A binary digit has an average surprisal of $1$ bit only when
its two values are equally likely;
a digit that is $0$ nine times in ten averages less.

:::
